title: Phase 03 — Foundations of Reasoning (6–10 years)
primaryObjective: Foundational knowledge, reasoning, and creativity — the child learns to read the world, ask good questions, and make things.
summary: In these years the child becomes a reader, a maker, and a reasoner. Rather than memorising facts for tests, the focus is learning how knowledge is built: observing, questioning, explaining, and creating. Reading, numbers, and first digital tools become instruments for curiosity. The platform supports caregivers and educators in keeping learning hands-on and tied to real life, while growing responsibility, friendship skills, and the ability to disagree kindly.
guidingPrinciple: Build thinkers, not reciters. The aim is not the right answer repeated back, but a child who can ask a good question, test an idea, and explain their reasoning.

developmentDomains.focus: Asking why and how, comparing ideas, spotting patterns, and explaining reasoning with evidence.
Fluent reading for meaning, writing to express ideas, listening, and respectful discussion.
Observing, asking testable questions, predicting, experimenting, and drawing conclusions from everyday phenomena.
Making, inventing, art, music, and imaginative projects that turn ideas into something real.
Friendship, cooperation, handling disagreement kindly, and seeing other points of view.
Responsibility for belongings and chores, time and task planning, and money basics in real contexts.
First, guided digital tools: safe searching, simple creation, and the idea that screens are tools, not masters.
Fairness, honesty, rules and why they exist, and caring for the shared spaces and people around them.

yearPlans.label: Age 6–7
objectives: Grow reading fluency and a love of stories and information.
Turn everyday curiosity into simple questions the child can investigate.
Build responsibility through real chores and caring for belongings.
Practise friendship skills: sharing, turn-taking, and settling disagreements.
capabilities: Reads simple texts for meaning and writes short sentences.
Counts, adds, and subtracts using real objects and situations.
Carries out a small daily responsibility independently.
Names others' feelings and begins to resolve conflicts with words.

yearPlans.label: Age 7–8
objectives: Read longer texts and explain what they mean in their own words.
Run simple, fair experiments: question, guess, test, and talk about results.
Introduce safe, guided use of digital tools for creating and finding things out.
Discuss fairness, honesty, and rules through real situations and stories.
capabilities: Summarises a story or article and asks questions about it.
Plans and runs a simple experiment and records what happened.
Uses a device with guidance to create or research something specific.
Explains why a rule is fair or unfair with a reason.

yearPlans.label: Age 9–10
objectives: Build independent projects that span several days or weeks.
Compare sources and begin to ask 'how do we know this is true?'
Manage simple budgets, time, and personal goals.
Take on roles that contribute to family, class, or community.
capabilities: Plans, carries out, and reflects on a multi-step project.
Questions where information comes from and checks it against another source.
Manages small amounts of money and plans how to use time.
Takes initiative to help and contribute without being asked.

daily.title: Read and retell
daily.description: Read something each day and explain it back in your own words, or ask one question about it, to turn reading into thinking.

daily.title: One real responsibility
daily.description: A daily job the child owns — feeding a pet, packing their bag, helping with a meal — building reliability and belonging.

daily.title: Question of the day
daily.description: Capture a real question the child wonders about and decide together how you could find out the answer.

weekly.title: Kitchen or backyard experiment
weekly.description: Pick a question (Which paper plane flies farthest? Does salt melt ice faster?), predict, test it fairly, and discuss the result.

weekly.title: Make something that works
weekly.description: Design and build a small working thing — a marble run, a simple circuit, a comic — and improve it after testing.

weekly.title: Fair-or-not debate
weekly.description: Discuss a real situation from the week and argue both sides kindly to practise reasoning and empathy.

parentGuidance.topic: Protect curiosity from the test mindset
parentGuidance.guidance: Praise effort, questions, and attempts rather than only correct answers. A child who feels safe to be wrong keeps thinking and exploring.
Set clear, calm limits and favour creating over passive watching. Explore and talk about what your child does online rather than only policing it.
Resist solving every problem. Ask 'what have you tried?' and give hints rather than answers, so the child builds persistence and problem-solving.

parentGuidance.topic: Partner with teachers, not replace them
parentGuidance.guidance: Use the platform to support what happens at school and home. For learning, attention, or wellbeing concerns, talk with teachers and professionals.

milestones.description: Reads for meaning and explains ideas in their own words
Plans and carries out a simple, fair investigation
Resolves many peer conflicts with words and sees other viewpoints
Uses guided digital tools safely to create or find information

safety.guidance: Keep devices in shared spaces, agree on what is okay to do and share, and make it safe to tell a trusted adult about anything upsetting online — without fear of losing the device.
As the child does more alone (walking to a friend's, staying briefly unsupervised), agree clear rules, check-ins, and what to do in an emergency.
Talk about treating others with respect online and offline, recognising bullying, and telling a trusted adult. Emphasise that reporting harm is brave, not tattling.
If a child seems anxious, withdrawn, or is being harmed, involve parents, teachers, and professionals. The platform guides; it never replaces human care.

outcomes: The child reads fluently for meaning and writes to express their own ideas.
The child can turn curiosity into a question and test it in a simple, fair way.
The child plans and completes a multi-step project and reflects on it.
The child uses digital tools safely and knows screens are tools, not masters.
The child takes responsibility and treats others, online and offline, with respect.

projects.title: Mini research-and-make project
projects.description: Pick a question the child cares about, research it from two sources, and make something that shares the answer — a poster, model, or short talk.

projects.title: Family mini-enterprise
projects.description: Plan and run a small stall or service (lemonade, cards, chores for neighbours), tracking simple costs, earnings, and what to give back.

projects.title: Build and improve
projects.description: Build a working contraption (marble run, simple circuit, paper bridge), test it, and redesign it to work better.

appFeatures.userJourney: A learner logs questions they wonder about, and the app suggests a safe, hands-on way to investigate one with a parent or teacher.
A child breaks a project into small steps with a caregiver, tracks progress, and reflects at the end on what they learned.
An educator assigns short, safe activities on searching, creating, and spotting unreliable information, with offline discussion prompts.
A parent sees how to extend classroom themes at home with real-life activities, reinforcing teachers rather than second-guessing them.
